title: System design: deploy and host models (3b1b style)

lines.text: Monday morning. The fraud team hands you a trained model: fraud-v7.
lines.say: Monday morning. The fraud team hands you a trained model: fraud v seven.

lines.text: By Friday it must answer every payment, in milliseconds. So must 200 other models.
lines.say: By Friday it must answer every payment, in milliseconds. So must two hundred other models.

lines.text: How do you host them? Let's design it.
First, requirements. Deploy a model, scale it, roll out versions safely, and share GPUs.
lines.say: First, requirements. Deploy a model, scale it, roll out versions safely, and share G P Us.

lines.text: Then four questions.
Online or batch? I assume online. So p99 is 50 milliseconds.
lines.say: Online or batch? I assume online. So p ninety-nine is fifty milliseconds.

lines.text: How much traffic? I assume 2,000 requests a second at peak.
lines.say: How much traffic? I assume two thousand requests a second at peak.

lines.text: One model or many? I assume 200 models, from 20 teams.
lines.say: One model or many? I assume two hundred models, from twenty teams.

lines.text: Classic models or LLMs? I assume classic first.
lines.say: Classic models or L L Ms? I assume classic first.

lines.text: I assume a number, say it aloud, and move on.
Now the numbers. One GPU serves 100 requests a second, one at a time. In batches of 16, 500. So I batch.
lines.say: Now the numbers. One G P U serves one hundred requests a second, one at a time. In batches of sixteen, five hundred. So I batch.

lines.text: 2,000 divided by 500 is 4 GPUs. I add half for a failed zone. Six.
lines.say: Two thousand divided by five hundred is four G P Us. I add half for a failed zone. Six.

lines.text: A GPU costs 2 dollars an hour. At full load, that is a tenth of a cent per thousand requests. At 30 percent load, over three times more. So utilization is the cost lever.
lines.say: A G P U costs two dollars an hour. At full load, that is a tenth of a cent per thousand requests. At thirty percent load, over three times more. So utilization is the cost lever.

lines.text: Last. A new replica loads 4 gigabytes, and needs 3 minutes. A spike does not wait. So I keep warm replicas.
lines.say: Last. A new replica loads four gigabytes, and needs three minutes. A spike does not wait. So I keep warm replicas.

lines.text: Decision one. Packaging. A container per model, or one shared inference server?
My call: a shared server, Triton. Models arrive as ONNX or TensorRT.
lines.say: My call: a shared server, Triton. Models arrive as onix, or Tensor R T.

lines.text: Because batching and GPU sharing are built once, in the server.
lines.say: Because batching and G P U sharing are built once, in the server.

lines.text: Not a container per model. Every team writes its own server, and each one holds a whole GPU.
lines.say: Not a container per model. Every team writes its own server, and each one holds a whole G P U.

lines.text: Unless the model needs custom Python code. That one gets its own container.
The proof. I moved a 120-GPU cluster, over 100,000 dollars a month, onto Triton. The ML team had to convert models from PyTorch to TensorRT.
lines.say: The proof. I moved a one hundred and twenty G P U cluster, over one hundred thousand dollars a month, onto Triton. The M L team had to convert models from Pie Torch to Tensor R T.

lines.text: So first I measured one model on Triton, to have a number before I asked anyone.
Two models in two months gave about 3x throughput. The rest of the migration funded itself.
lines.say: Two models in two months gave about three times the throughput. The rest of the migration funded itself.

lines.text: Decision two. One model per GPU, or many models packed on one?
lines.say: Decision two. One model per G P U, or many models packed on one?

lines.text: My call: pack the small models together. Big ones get their own GPU.
lines.say: My call: pack the small models together. Big ones get their own G P U.

lines.text: Because most of the 200 models are idle most of the day.
lines.say: Because most of the two hundred models are idle most of the day.

lines.text: Not a GPU for every model. It isolates well. But I pay for idle GPUs.
lines.say: Not a G P U for every model. It isolates well. But I pay for idle G P Us.

lines.text: Unless the model is on the payment path, like fraud-v7. A noisy neighbour breaks its 50 milliseconds. So it gets dedicated GPUs.
lines.say: Unless the model is on the payment path, like fraud v seven. A noisy neighbour breaks its fifty milliseconds. So it gets dedicated G P Us.

lines.text: Decision three. When do I add replicas? On CPU, or on queue depth?
lines.say: Decision three. When do I add replicas? On C P U, or on queue depth?

lines.text: My call: scale on requests in flight. And never below two warm replicas.
Because the work is on the GPU. CPU stays flat while the queue grows.
lines.say: Because the work is on the G P U. C P U stays flat while the queue grows.

lines.text: Not CPU scaling. It reacts late. And not scale to zero. The first request would wait 3 minutes.
lines.say: Not C P U scaling. It reacts late. And not scale to zero. The first request would wait three minutes.

lines.text: Unless it is a batch model. Nobody waits. It scales to zero.
Decision four. How does version 7 replace version 6? In one step, or in stages?
lines.say: Decision four. How does version seven replace version six? In one step, or in stages?

lines.text: My call: stages. Shadow, then a canary at 5 percent, then everyone. With automatic rollback.
lines.say: My call: stages. Shadow, then a canary at five percent, then everyone. With automatic rollback.

lines.text: Because a model can be healthy as a service, and wrong as a model. In the canary, latency is fine. Errors are fine. But it blocks three times more payments.
So the gate watches a quality metric too. It rolls back by itself. Version 6 is still in the registry, unchanged.
lines.say: So the gate watches a quality metric too. It rolls back by itself. Version six is still in the registry, unchanged.

lines.text: Not one step. It is fast. But every customer gets the bad model.
Unless the model has no live users.
Follow-ups. One team floods the platform. What happens?
Each team has a quota and its own queue. Over quota, only that team is rejected.
How is an LLM different?
lines.say: How is an L L M different?

lines.text: Tokens stream back. The server is vLLM, with continuous batching. And capacity is tokens per second.
lines.say: Tokens stream back. The server is V L L M, with continuous batching. And capacity is tokens per second.

lines.text: Self-host the LLM, or call an API?
lines.say: Self-host the L L M, or call an A P I?

lines.text: Both. I self-host a small Qwen model for one narrow text decision, next to a frontier model API. My rule: below about a third of the volume, do not self-host.
lines.say: Both. I self-host a small Kwen model for one narrow text decision, next to a frontier model A P I. My rule: below about a third of the volume, do not self-host.

lines.text: The registry goes down. Does serving stop?
No. Replicas already hold their weights. Only new deploys wait.
So, the design.
Immutable versions, on a shared inference server.
Small models packed on shared GPUs. Critical ones alone.
lines.say: Small models packed on shared G P Us. Critical ones alone.

lines.text: Scale on queue depth, with warm replicas.
Shadow, canary, everyone, with automatic rollback.
The bad version reached 5 percent of payments. Not all of them.
lines.say: The bad version reached five percent of payments. Not all of them.
